title: Start from zero
blurb: Never written a line of code? Begin here. You learn how computers run programs, the terminal, your first language, and how web pages are made. Then you pick a direction.
outcome: You can write small programs, use Git, and build a simple web page.

stages.title: Find your feet
stages.why: The words, the terminal and the tools every developer uses daily.

stages.title: Your first language
stages.why: Python reads almost like English, so you learn programming and not punctuation.

stages.title: Your first web page
stages.why: Something you can see and show to people.

title: Frontend developer
blurb: Build what people see and touch: pages, layouts and interactive applications in the browser.
outcome: You can build a responsive, interactive web application with React and Next.js.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.why: The terminal and Git are part of every job.

stages.title: The web platform
stages.why: Every framework produces HTML and CSS in the end.

stages.title: JavaScript
stages.why: The language that makes pages do things.

stages.title: Applications
stages.why: Components, state and routing for real products.

title: Backend developer
blurb: Build what happens behind the screen: APIs, databases, authentication and services that stay up.
outcome: You can design, build, test and ship an API with a database behind it.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.why: The terminal and Git are part of every job.

stages.title: A first language
stages.why: A language for thinking in before you specialise.

stages.title: Data
stages.why: Almost every backend is a careful way of reading and writing data.

stages.title: Services
stages.why: HTTP, APIs, authentication and structure.

stages.title: Shipping
stages.why: Code is finished when it runs somewhere other than your laptop.

title: Full-stack developer
blurb: Both sides: the interface in the browser and the server and database behind it. The broadest path.
outcome: You can build and deploy a complete web application on your own.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.why: The terminal and Git are part of every job.

stages.title: The web platform
stages.why: Structure, style and the language of the browser.

stages.title: The interface
stages.why: Components and state.

stages.title: The server
stages.why: APIs and the database they talk to.

stages.title: The whole product
stages.why: One framework for both sides, packaged to run anywhere.

title: DevOps engineer
blurb: Get software from a commit to production, keep it running, and automate everything in between.
outcome: You can containerise a system, build its pipeline, deploy it safely and watch it in production.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.why: You will live in the terminal.

stages.title: A scripting language
stages.why: For everything that outgrows a shell script.

stages.title: Containers
stages.why: The unit that everything is shipped in.

stages.title: Pipelines and operations
stages.why: Build, release, deploy, observe.

stages.title: The services you will run
stages.why: Know the databases you are responsible for.

title: Game developer
blurb: Make things move: game loops, input, collisions and the mathematics behind them.
outcome: You can build a complete 2D game, and you understand what a game engine does for you.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.why: The terminal and Git are part of every job.

stages.title: Programming
stages.why: Games in the browser are written in JavaScript.

stages.title: Games
stages.why: The loop, movement, collisions, state, a finished game.

stages.title: Under the hood
stages.why: Path finding, performance, and the languages engines are written in.

title: Systems programmer
blurb: Close to the machine: memory, performance, concurrency, and the languages operating systems and databases are built in.
outcome: You understand how programs use memory and processors, in C, Rust and Go.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.why: The terminal and Git are part of every job.

stages.title: The machine
stages.why: C shows you memory and pointers with nothing hidden.

stages.title: Algorithms
stages.why: The difference between fast and impossible.

stages.title: Modern systems languages
stages.why: Safety without a garbage collector, and concurrency made simple.

title: AI application engineer
blurb: Build products on top of large language models: prompts, tools, agents and retrieval, with solid engineering around them.
outcome: You can build, evaluate and ship an application that uses a language model.

stages.title: Foundations
stages.why: The terminal and Git are part of every job.

stages.title: Python
stages.why: The language of the AI ecosystem.

stages.title: Language models
stages.why: From a first API call to agents and retrieval.

stages.title: Data and speed
stages.why: Where the documents live, and how to cache expensive calls.

stages.title: Shipping
stages.why: An API around your model, in a container.
